explanation: Binary-search an inclusive candidate interval. Save an index whenever the middle equals k, then continue strictly to its left to seek an earlier equal value. Return the saved index or -1.
timeComplexity: O(log n). Each iteration halves the candidate interval, hence logarithmically many comparisons.
spaceComplexity: O(1). Only two endpoints, a midpoint and possibly one saved index are retained.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/search_first_key.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: The saved result is an occurrence of k, and any earlier occurrence remains in the candidate interval. A value below k excludes its entire left side; a value above k excludes its right side. On equality, keeping only the left side cannot discard an earlier answer. Exhaustion therefore leaves the first occurrence saved.
walkthrough: For [-2,1,1,1,5] and k=1, middle 2 matches: save 2 and search [0,1]. Middle 0 is below 1, so move left to 1. Middle 1 matches: save 1 and finish. Return 1.
edgeCases: Repeated targets return their first index.
A lower bound at array length means the target is absent.
Targets below the minimum still require an equality check.
